authorities.title_or_locator: Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable
26EC22, complete paragraphs 10–13, including omitted paragraphs and associated footnotes
Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds, section 6.8 and applicable scope provisions
Footnote 2 associated with the ownership-record and operational-compatibility provision
Parts A and B of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular and its intermediary scope provisions
Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds, section 6.11C and applicable valuation scope

claims.action: Retain ultimate responsibility for management and operational soundness of the adopted tokenisation arrangement
claims.statement: Product Providers should remain ultimately responsible for management and operational soundness of the adopted tokenisation arrangement.
uncertainty: The provision assigns responsibility but does not specify a complete test of adequate supervision or soundness.

claims.action: Retain ultimate responsibility for ownership record keeping
claims.statement: Product Providers should remain ultimately responsible for ownership record keeping.

claims.action: Retain full responsibility despite outsourcing
conditions: Including outsourcing arrangements such as those envisaged under section 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds
claims.statement: Outsourcing does not displace the Product Provider's full responsibility; footnote 1 links this responsibility to public offerings in Hong Kong and the importance of proper ownership records.
uncertainty: Retention of responsibility does not itself establish that every operational function or decision must be performed personally by the Product Provider.

claims.action: Refer to applicable factors in Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular
claims.statement: Footnote 1 directs reference to Part A's applicable factors when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.
uncertainty: The factors and their applicability are not supplied.

claims.action: Ensure maintenance of proper records of token holders' ownership interests
claims.statement: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders' ownership interests in the product are maintained.
uncertainty: The applicable criteria for proper records and omitted footnote 2 remain to be checked.

claims.action: Ensure operational compatibility with involved service providers
claims.statement: Product Providers should ensure that the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with the service providers involved.
uncertainty: Actual compatibility cannot be established from the provision alone.

claims.action: Confirm management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity
claims.statement: Paragraph 14 states that Product Providers should confirm management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; the request phrase most directly modifies demonstration.
temporal: No express SFC-request trigger for confirmation
uncertainty: Whether the SFC-satisfaction standard also grammatically qualifies confirmation is not explicit.

claims.action: Demonstrate management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity to the SFC's satisfaction
claims.statement: Upon SFC request, Product Providers should demonstrate to the SFC's satisfaction the three stated objects: arrangement management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping, and smart-contract integrity.
uncertainty: Footnote 5 restates demonstration without repeating the request qualifier.

claims.action: Confirm and demonstrate compliance with paragraphs 10–13 as a minimum
conditions: As minimum content of confirmation and demonstration under paragraph 14
claims.statement: Footnote 5 makes compliance with paragraphs 10–13 minimum content of what Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC.
uncertainty: Complete paragraphs 10–13 are not supplied.
The footnote may elaborate the parent paragraph's request-conditioned demonstration or, read independently, state an unqualified demonstration expectation.

claims.action: Confirm and demonstrate with a high level of confidence that smart contracts have no contract vulnerabilities or security flaws
conditions: As minimum content specified by footnote 5
claims.statement: Footnote 5 requires confirmation and demonstration that smart contracts are not subject to contract vulnerabilities or security flaws, with a high level of confidence.
uncertainty: The confidence phrase most directly concerns the smart-contract assurance; a broader reading covering the combined compliance and smart-contract demonstration is also possible.
No confidence metric or testing standard is supplied.

claims.action: Obtain third-party audit or verification of the specified arrangement, records and smart contracts
claims.statement: Paragraph 15 calls for obtaining third-party audit or verification of arrangement management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity upon SFC request.
uncertainty: Obtaining an audit or verification does not by itself establish fulfilment of the underlying substantive requirements.

claims.action: Obtain a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application
claims.statement: Paragraph 16 calls for obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion to support the application upon SFC request.
uncertainty: The excerpt does not specify the opinion's required issues or expressly identify who determines satisfactoriness.

claims.action: Maintain a register of holders
claims.actor: The scheme or, for a unit trust, the trustee or person appointed by the trustee
claims.statement: Section 6.8 requires the scheme or, for a unit trust, the trustee or its appointed person to maintain a register of holders.
uncertainty: The allocation of register maintenance does not resolve whether the Product Provider has fulfilled its separate retained responsibility.

claims.action: Advise the Commission of the addresses where the register is kept
claims.actor: Responsible register-maintenance party; the sentence uses passive wording
claims.statement: The Commission must be advised on request of the addresses where the register is kept.
uncertainty: The sentence does not expressly name the notifying actor.

claims.action: Exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in selecting, appointing and monitoring a third-party valuer
conditions: A third party is engaged in scheme valuation
claims.statement: Section 6.11C requires reasonable care, skill and diligence in selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring to ensure the third-party valuer has knowledge, experience and resources appropriate to each scheme's valuation policies and procedures.
uncertainty: This express valuation standard is not automatically a tokenisation supervision standard.

claims.action: Subject third-party valuation activities to ongoing supervision and periodic review
conditions: A third party is engaged in scheme valuation
claims.statement: Third-party valuation activities should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.
uncertainty: Direct application to tokenisation requires an applicable scope or incorporation basis.

claims.action: Remain responsible for overall operation of the tokenisation arrangement despite outsourcing
claims.actor: Intermediaries issuing or substantially involved in issuance of Tokenised Securities
conditions: They intend to deal in or advise on those Tokenised Securities
claims.statement: The intermediary circular states that qualifying issuers or substantially involved intermediaries remain responsible for overall tokenisation operation notwithstanding outsourcing.
uncertainty: Application depends on the Product Provider also satisfying the stated intermediary and activity conditions.

claims.action: Conduct due diligence on issuers, involved vendors and service providers, and tokenisation features and risks
conditions: Dealing in, advising on, or managing portfolios investing in Tokenised Securities
claims.statement: Paragraph 17 reminds intermediaries undertaking the specified activities to conduct due diligence on the relevant issuers, vendors, service providers, and tokenisation features and risks.
uncertainty: The text uses a reminder rather than an express must or should; SHOULD represents its directive character.
Application to the Product Provider depends on its role and activities.

claims.action: Understand and be satisfied with issuer and vendor controls for ownership and technology risks
conditions: Engaging in related Tokenised Securities activities
claims.statement: Intermediaries should understand and be satisfied with controls implemented by issuers and their vendors or service providers to manage ownership and technology risks before engaging in related activities.
uncertainty: Intermediary satisfaction with controls is distinct from demonstration to the SFC's satisfaction under paragraph 14.

claims.action: Refer to the non-exhaustive factors in Parts A and B of the Appendix
conditions: Within the intermediary provisions' applicable scope
claims.statement: The intermediary provisions direct reference to Parts A and B of the Appendix for a non-exhaustive list of consideration factors.
uncertainty: Footnote 1 refers specifically to Part A; this separate reference does not automatically import Part B into the Product Provider requirement.

uncertainties: Retention of ultimate responsibility, allocation of operational authority, actual supervisory conduct, and sound operational or record-keeping outcomes are distinct. The excerpts do not make any one of these conclusive proof of the others.

An assessment of fulfilment requires an applicable standard and actual evidence of the arrangement, authority allocation, supervision, records, operational compatibility and smart-contract assurance. Neither a contractual reservation of responsibility nor favourable outcomes alone are specified as a sufficient test.

The supplied text does not settle whether paragraph 10 imposes an outcome-based responsibility, a responsibility discharged through adequate management and supervision, or a combination. Its express operational and record-keeping objects prevent reducing the assessment solely to formal allocation of authority.
Section 6.11C supplies an express care, skill, diligence and supervision standard for valuation. Importing that standard into paragraph 10 without an applicability basis would be unsupported.

On the integrated reading of paragraph 14 and footnote 5, confirmation remains expected without an SFC request, while demonstration is request-triggered. Footnote 5 elaborates minimum content and assurance. Its unqualified wording also supports a rival reading of an independent demonstration expectation; the supplied excerpts do not conclusively resolve that tension.

The SFC-satisfaction phrase most directly attaches to demonstration. Footnote 5 directs both confirmation and demonstration to the SFC. The high-confidence phrase most directly qualifies assurance about smart-contract vulnerabilities and flaws, but may qualify the combined assurance statement. No operational measure of either standard is supplied.

Without an SFC request, the express triggers in paragraphs 15 and 16 have not occurred, and under the integrated reading neither has paragraph 14's demonstration trigger. This does not remove confirmation or substantive responsibilities, prove compliance, or establish that no other applicable provision requires evidence.

Paragraph 15 concerns obtaining third-party audit or verification of the stated technical and record-keeping objects; paragraph 16 concerns obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. Neither is expressly an automatic substitute for paragraph 14's confirmation and demonstration.

The omitted paragraphs, footnote 2, applicable Appendix factors, scope provisions, actual SFC requests and case facts are needed before reaching a compliance conclusion. No deadline, evidentiary safe harbour or exhaustive supervisory checklist is established by the supplied excerpts.
No separate questions, concerns or output_identity_contract objects were supplied beyond the selected_slice; its issues are addressed through the claims and uncertainties.

units.rationale: Core retained-responsibility provision; separates arrangement soundness and ownership records from the effect of outsourcing.
Qualifies responsibility despite outsourcing and supplies public-offering context and an applicable Appendix dependency.
States substantive record-maintenance and operational-compatibility expectations relevant to fulfilment.
Separates confirmation from request-triggered demonstration and identifies their objects and satisfaction standard.
Adds minimum assurance content and high confidence while creating a potential trigger-attachment ambiguity.
Distinct request-triggered third-party audit or verification expectation.
Distinct request-triggered satisfactory legal-opinion expectation supporting the application.
Identifies the register-maintenance actors contemplated by the footnote's section 6.8 reference.
Repeats register maintenance and adds a separate request-conditioned address notification; neither displaces retained responsibility.
Express valuation supervision comparator with different modalities; its standard cannot automatically be transferred to tokenisation.
Potentially overlapping intermediary responsibility depends on issuance involvement and intended activities.
Conditional intermediary due diligence and prior control satisfaction may qualify the assessment; Appendix references have their own scope.
